Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Rust web application. Start in the `/app` Git repository: it has a minimal Cargo project (`quizzy`) and no app yet. Rust (stable), Cargo, SQLite (the library and the CLI), and Chromium are installed. You can download crates from crates.io; other network access is blocked. Fetch and build all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the build, the database, and so on) and runs the app in release mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`. It must work offline (for example, `cargo build --release --offline`), and it should start in a few minutes at most.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Quizzy runs quizzes during conference talks. A moderator shows the questions on the big screen, and the audience answers on their phones. The first release covers the moderator's side: preparing quizzes.

The design is in `docs/mockups/`, exported from our design tool: a style guide and two screens of this release (the quiz page and the question form), each as a static HTML page (open it in a browser) and a PNG. The stylesheet and the font next to them are the design's assets: use them as they are or adapt them. Follow the look: colors, typography, pill buttons, and layout. Big-screen pages run on LED walls and projectors; player pages run on phones.

The moderator area lives under `/moderate`. Every page in it requires HTTP Basic authentication with the credentials from `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`. Missing or wrong credentials get `401`.

Quizzes:

- `/moderate` lists the quizzes and has the "New quiz" button.
- The quiz form has one field, "Title" (required), and the "Save quiz" button. Saving opens the quiz page.
- The quiz page shows the title and the questions in order. It has the "Add question" button, the "Settings" link and the "Preview" link.
- "Settings" opens the same quiz form for the quiz, and the "Delete quiz" button, which asks for confirmation.

Questions are single-choice with text options. The question form has:

- "Question": the question text (required)
- option rows: each row has a text field labelled "Option 1", "Option 2", and so on, and a checkbox labelled "Option 1 is correct", "Option 2 is correct", and so on. A new question starts with four empty rows. The "Add option" button adds one more row with the next number.
- "Active": a checkbox, on by default
- the "Save question" button

Rules for options:

- Empty rows are skipped.
- A question needs at least two options. Otherwise the form shows "Add at least two options".
- At least one option must be correct (several correct options are fine). Otherwise the form shows "Mark at least one option as correct".
- When a rule fails, nothing is saved and the form keeps what the moderator typed.

Each question on the quiz page shows its text and its options, with the correct options marked. It also has:

- "Move up" and "Move down" buttons that change the order
- the "Active" checkbox: changing it saves at once, with no extra button
- the "Edit" link to the question form
- the "Delete" button, which asks for confirmation

Inactive questions stay on the quiz page, but the preview skips them.

The preview lets the moderator try the quiz as a player would. It goes through the active questions in order, one at a time:

- It shows the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options as buttons.
- Picking an option shows "Correct!" or "Wrong!" and reveals the correct options.
- The "Next question" button opens the next question. After the last question, the "See score" button shows the result, for example "Score: 2/3".
- The "Start over" button restarts the preview. Preview answers are not stored anywhere.

# Quizzy — implementation notes

These notes capture the design decisions of the first release (moderator side)
so future steps (live runs, player pages, big-screen presentation) can build on
them.

## Stack

- **Rust (edition 2024), no async runtime.** The app uses `tiny_http` (one
  thread per request) + `rusqlite` against the system SQLite. This keeps the
  release build small and fast and works fully offline.
- **Templates are plain `format!` strings** in `src/views.rs`, with a small
  HTML-escaping helper. No template engine, no client-side framework.
- **All assets are embedded** in the binary (`include_str!` / `include_bytes!`)
  and served from `/static/*`: the design's `quizzy.css` and the Inter woff2
  font from `docs/mockups/` live in `static/`.
- **Dependencies are vendored** in `vendor/` and wired up through
  `.cargo/config.toml` (`source.crates-io` → `vendored-sources`), so
  `cargo build --release --offline` works even with an empty `CARGO_HOME`.

## Running

`bin/serve` creates `storage/`, runs
`cargo build --release --offline --locked` and then execs
`target/release/quizzy` in the foreground. It reads `PORT`,
`QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` (and optionally
`QUIZZY_STORAGE_DIR`, default `storage`). The app binds `0.0.0.0:$PORT`, speaks
plain HTTP, accepts any `Host`, and exposes `GET /up` for readiness checks.

## Data model

`storage/quizzy.sqlite3`, three tables, foreign keys on and deletes cascade:

- `quizzes (id, title, created_at)`
- `questions (id, quiz_id, body, is_active, position, created_at)`
- `options (id, question_id, body, is_correct, position)`

Question order is `position`; new questions get `MAX(position)+1`. Move
up/down swaps the two neighbouring positions. Options are ordered by position
and stored without empty rows (the form skips them).

## Routes

Moderator pages all live under `/moderate` and require HTTP Basic auth
(`401` + `WWW-Authenticate` otherwise):

| Method | Path                                             | Purpose                          |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/moderate`                                       | quiz list + "New quiz"           |
| GET    | `/moderate/quizzes/new`                           | new quiz form                    |
| POST   | `/moderate/quizzes`                               | create quiz, redirects to quiz   |
| GET    | `/moderate/quizzes/{id}`                          | quiz page (questions in order)   |
| GET    | `/moderate/quizzes/{id}/edit`                     | settings form + delete quiz      |
| POST   | `/moderate/quizzes/{id}`                          | rename quiz                      |
| POST   | `/moderate/quizzes/{id}/delete`                   | delete quiz (confirm in browser) |
| GET    | `/moderate/quizzes/{id}/questions/new`            | question form (4 empty rows)     |
| POST   | `/moderate/quizzes/{id}/questions`                | create question                  |
| GET    | `/moderate/quizzes/{id}/questions/{qid}/edit`     | edit question                    |
| POST   | `/moderate/quizzes/{id}/questions/{qid}`          | save question                    |
| POST   | `/moderate/quizzes/{id}/questions/{qid}/delete`   | delete question                  |
| POST   | `/moderate/quizzes/{id}/questions/{qid}/move`     | reorder (direction=up/down)      |
| POST   | `/moderate/quizzes/{id}/questions/{qid}/active`   | toggle Active at once            |
| GET    | `/moderate/quizzes/{id}/preview`                  | preview                          |
| POST   | `/moderate/quizzes/{id}/preview/answer`           | pick an option                   |
| POST   | `/moderate/quizzes/{id}/preview/next`             | next active question             |
| POST   | `/moderate/quizzes/{id}/preview/score`            | score + "Start over"             |

## Question form rules

- Fields arrive as `question`, `option_N`, `correct_N`, `active`.
- The server derives the submitted row numbers from the keys, so it preserves
  however many rows the moderator had after "Add option" when validation fails.
- Empty (whitespace-only) rows are skipped; a `correct_N` on an empty row is
  ignored.
- Errors (rendered above the form) are "Question is required",
  "Add at least two options" and "Mark at least one option is correct".
  Nothing is written to the database when any of them fires.

## Preview state

Preview answers are deliberately *not stored anywhere*: every preview page
carries the chosen option list in a hidden `<input name="answers">` field
(CSV of option indexes), so the score is recomputed from the render-time
question list. The preview only ever reads active questions, ordered by
position, which is why deactivating a question removes it from preview while
leaving it on the quiz page.

Everything is complete and verified. Here's a summary of what was built:

## Quizzy moderator app

**Stack**: Rust + `tiny_http` + `rusqlite` (system SQLite), server-rendered HTML using the design's CSS/font assets. No async runtime, no external template engine — small and fast.

**Entry point**: `bin/serve` creates `storage/`, builds `cargo build --release --offline --locked`, and execs the app in the foreground on `0.0.0.0:$PORT`. Dependencies are vendored in `vendor/` with `.cargo/config.toml` source replacement, so a cold network-free build works (verified with an empty `CARGO_HOME`; ~4s, ~1.3MB binary).

**Features implemented**
- `/up` readiness endpoint (public); all `/moderate` pages behind HTTP Basic auth (401 + `WWW-Authenticate` otherwise).
- Quiz list with **New quiz**, quiz create/edit/delete forms (**Title** required, **Save quiz**, **Delete quiz** with native `confirm()`), quiz page with ordered questions, **Add question**, **Settings**, **Preview**.
- Question form: **Question** textarea, four default option rows labelled **Option 1..4** with real checkboxes labelled **Option 1 is correct..**, JS **Add option** (adds **Option 5**, etc.), **Active** on by default, **Save question**. Empty rows skipped; errors **Add at least two options** / **Mark at least one option as correct** preserve typed input and save nothing.
- Quiz page: option lists with correct answers marked, **Move up**/**Move down**, instant-save **Active** checkbox, **Edit**, **Delete** with native confirm.
- Preview: active questions only, one at a time, **Question 1 of 3** progress, option buttons, **Correct!**/**Wrong!** with correct options revealed, **Next question**, **See score** (**Score: 2/3**), **Start over**. Answers travel in hidden fields only—never stored.
- Data lives in `storage/quizzy.sqlite3`; no external calls. Design notes are in `docs/notes.md`.

**Verification**: 136 HTTP checks and 47 headless-Chromium browser checks (Basic auth, Add option JS, checkbox auto-save, native confirm dialogs, full preview journey) all pass; restart persistence, multiple-correct options, edge moves, any-Host plain-HTTP behavior, and cold offline serving were also verified.
